name: Residential Electrical Contractors
purpose: AhernAI sales discovery and illustrative configuration guidance
summary: For residential electricians. Clarify mains electrical work versus smart-home, AV or network installation. Explore estimate requests and office coordination without technical diagnosis. Ask one useful question at a time about the caller's actual workflow. Explain Level 1 when messages and FAQs fit; move directly to Level 2 when the caller needs routine work completed. Recommend the lowest suitable level as soon as the need is understood; no mandatory three-level tour. Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.
discovery_questions: Is your main work residential electrical service, installations or a different specialty?
Which types of calls interrupt your team most often?
What happens when someone calls while everyone is at a job?
What details does your office need before accepting a request?
Which requests can be booked directly, and which need an electrician's review first?
Where do you currently keep appointments and customer requests?
Who should handle complaints or requests outside your approved service scope?

levels.name: Answering Service
use_cases: Answer approved hours, service-area and accepted-work questions without assessing installations or interpreting electrical requirements.
Collect contact details, property location and the caller's estimate or service request for human review.
Send a reason-for-call summary to one agreed destination while the crew is unavailable, preserving the office's control over scheduling.
levels.probe: Would consistent request capture be enough, or does the caller need another step during the call?
fit_signals: Missed calls and incomplete voicemail details are the main problem.
A qualified person must review every job before scheduling.

levels.name: Receptionist
use_cases: Qualify requests against approved service areas and job categories, then offer screened transfers where human judgment is needed.
Book or change eligible estimate appointments and update the agreed customer or job system using verified availability and configured automation.
Collect approved project details and route estimate requests to the office, keeping safety concerns and technical decisions with qualified staff.
levels.probe: Which estimate requests can follow standard booking rules?
fit_signals: The caller needs routine receptionist work completed rather than only a message.
Approved business rules and verified systems support the agreed workflow.

levels.name: Manager
use_cases: Collect detailed complaints about a prior service experience and the requested resolution for an authorized human, without deciding fault.
Explain approved estimate, appointment-change and follow-up policies while sending exceptions and financial questions to the business owner.

Support approved employee coordination, such as recording a shift callout or coverage request and routing it to the authorized supervisor. Employment, staffing approval, disciplinary, financial and policy-exception decisions remain human; do not request medical reasons or other sensitive employee details.
levels.probe: Only after the caller raises a management need: Which situations should the agent handle under approved rules, and which should reach you?
fit_signals: The caller asks for help with difficult or disgruntled callers and escalations.
The caller wants approved employee coordination or supervisory support.

scope_boundaries: Do not diagnose electrical hazards, provide DIY wiring or repair instructions, interpret code compliance, certify safety or promise that a described job is suitable.

For an immediate safety concern, stop the sales discussion and refer at a high level to appropriate local emergency services or a qualified human. Do not troubleshoot or instruct the caller to test equipment.
No promised emergency response, dispatch, arrival, price, refund, discount or policy exception. Human financial and technical decisions remain with the business; examples do not perform live actions.

Level 1 captures approved FAQs, caller details and a summary to one destination; it does not book, submit orders, update a CRM or make screened transfers. Level 2 covers agreed routine receptionist duties and supporting automation. Package fit is based on duties, not a one-calendar/one-CRM or two-integration quota. Scope is agreed before launch; this is not an unlimited software-development commitment.

Routine receptionist duties and the supporting automation are included in the agreed Level 2 scope, without an additional AhernAI automation or integration-build charge. Confirm software compatibility, access, allowed actions and failure handling during setup; an unverified connection is not an automatic surcharge.

Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.

Do not promise that a named app or POS is supported merely because the caller names it. Verify compatibility during setup and agree a workable destination or fallback; disclose any actual work outside the agreed duties before proceeding.
setup_requirements: Confirm business specialty, approved work categories, service area, hours, FAQs and one summary destination.
Document what may be booked, what requires technical review, calendar permissions and staff transfer or escalation availability.
Confirm compatible systems, the agreed receptionist duties and fallback behavior; approve and test the configured call paths before launch.
Agree the routine duties and supporting automation included in the package, approved actions, access permissions, successful completion signals and failure paths before launch.

adjacent_services.trigger: The business needs broader back-office work beyond its agreed receptionist duties.
adjacent_services.example: Explore a separate project only for that broader need. Automation needed for agreed Level 2 receptionist work is already included; do not resell it as a Quickstart or add-on.

adjacent_services.trigger: The owner says the website does not explain accepted work or capture inquiries.
adjacent_services.example: Discuss clear service pages and an inquiry form based on the business's actual service scope.
